SK3532 The ref struct owns a disposable and cannot declare it

A ref struct constructs a field whose ref struct type is disposable through the pattern rule alone, and declares no Dispose() of its own.

CategoryLifetime
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

This is the one ownership shape the rest of the family cannot reach. A ref struct whose only disposal contract is a public parameterless Dispose() is disposable through the language's pattern rule and through nothing else — it implements no interface, so SK3502, which asks whether the owner implements the contract the field offers, has no contract to ask about and stays silent by construction. The owner constructs the resource, holds it, and offers its own callers no using to write: the release simply never happens, and no analyzer in the family reports it.

Example

Instead of:

ref struct Session {
    Lease lease;

    public Session(int size) {
        lease = new Lease(size);
    }
}

Write:

ref struct Session {
    Lease lease;

    public Session(int size) {
        lease = new Lease(size);
    }

    public void Dispose() {
        lease.Dispose();
    }
}

When it does not fire

⚠ The field's type must implement neither `IDisposable` nor `IAsyncDisposable`, and that is the disjointness guard rather than a limitation. C# 13 lets a ref struct implement an interface, and where the field's type does, the ownership is one SK3502 can see and report; without the test both rules would speak about one field. supersedes is the wrong instrument for that — Supersession.Apply suppresses the superseded finding on a shared span — so the two are made disjoint by construction and a fixture pins it. ⚠ Ownership is proved, not assumed: the field must be assigned from a direct object creation, in its own initializer or in a constructor. A field assigned from a constructor parameter is a borrowed resource whose lifetime belongs to the caller, and disposing it here would close something somebody else is still holding. ⚠ The disposal contract asked for is exactly the one using binds to: a public, parameterless, non-static Dispose() returning void. A type declaring only Dispose(bool) is reported, because using cannot bind to it. ⚠ Partial types are skipped, because the other half may carry the Dispose and is not in this tree. ⚠ No fix. A correct Dispose() decides which fields it releases, in what order, and whether a second call is safe — and the repair may instead be that this type should not own the resource at all. No edit answers that.
